title: ci-cd-rollback-breadcrumbs-notes-4
content:
Context:
- Quick personal breadcrumbs for the canary rollback we did on 2024-11-03 (svc: model-proxy / deployment: model-proxy-main).
- Incident: canary started returning 503s + elevated latency at ~09:12 UTC after a small image push (tag v2.14.1-canary).
- Goal: capture commands tried, failure signatures, hypotheses, and next steps so SRE/release team can reproduce or continue debugging.

Timeline / immediate actions taken:
- 09:10 - deploy CI pushed image ghcr.io/redwood-inference/model-proxy:v2.14.1-canary -> rollout started via argo/helm pipeline.
- 09:12 - alert: canary route 10% started seeing 503s, p95 latency jumped from ~120ms -> 1.2s.
- 09:13 - scaled canary down from 10% -> 0% in routing layer (console), but pods already created and some traffic persisted.
- 09:14 - initiated rollback to previous stable image v2.14.0 (helm rollback and kubectl rollout undo attempted).

Commands & outputs (raw snippets):
- kubectl get deployments -n prod
  model-proxy-main  3/3  Ready  2  6m

- kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep model-proxy
  model-proxy-main-5f8d6  2/2  Running  0  5m  10.10.5.12
  model-proxy-canary-7c9b0  1/2  CrashLoopBackOff  3  3m  10.10.6.8

- kubectl logs model-proxy-canary-7c9b0 -n prod -c model-proxy
  ERROR connecting to upstream: dial tcp 10.11.0.22:8080: connection refused
  2024-11-03T09:12:17Z [WARN] healthcheck: failed liveness check

- docker inspect ghcr.io/redwood-inference/model-proxy:v2.14.1-canary -> image config shows CMD ["/bin/model-proxy", "--pool-size=50"]
- docker inspect ghcr.io/redwood-inference/model-proxy:v2.14.0 -> CMD ["/bin/model-proxy", "--pool-size=20"]
  NOTE: pool-size change is suspicious.

- aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name release-artifacts --image-ids imageTag=v2.14.1-canary
  -> returned image manifest with digest sha256:abc123...
- curl -sSf https://registry.redwood-inference.com/v2/model-proxy/manifests/v2.14.1-canary | jq -r '.config.digest'
  -> "sha256:abc123..." (matches)

- kubectl describe pod model-proxy-canary-7c9b0 -n prod
  Events:
    Failed to pull image "ghcr.io/redwood-inference/model-proxy:v2.14.1-canary": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to resolve image reference
    Back-off pulling image
  BUT later logs show container started and then upstream connection refused -> suggests image pulled ok for at least some replicas.

- curl -I http://10.10.6.8:8080/health (from bastion)
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  uptime: 30s
  but proxy routes to upstream service-service:8080 which returns connection refused when probed from inside pod namespace.

Investigation notes + hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Config/flag change in v2.14.1-canary (--pool-size=50) increased concurrency and exposed connection exhaustion on upstream (model-server) -> results in refused connections.
- Hypothesis B: New image accidentally bundled wrong env defaults (e.g., wrong UPSTREAM_HOST or port) and tries connecting to a different internal IP that isn't serving.
- Hypothesis C: Race condition triggered by new init ordering; canary startup sequence differs, upstream short-lived failures cause readiness to flip resulting in 503s.
- Hypothesis D: Sidecar/iptables rules changed in the image (unlikely, but a binary build step might've altered net config).

Quick checks to validate hypotheses (commands tried and outcomes):
- exec into canary pod: kubectl exec -it model-proxy-canary-7c9b0 -n prod -- /bin/sh\  -> checked /etc/hosts, env vars, UPSTREAM_HOST env = service-service (correct), UPSTREAM_PORT = 8080.
- nc -vz service-service 8080 -> connection refused from inside pod.
- wget http://10.11.0.22:8080/health -> connection refused - matches logs.
- Checked model-server deployment logs around same time: model-server had multiple ooms and restarts due to psql pool exhaustion (db pool max hit). Pattern suggests the proxy increase in concurrency exacerbated model-server capacity.

Rollback steps taken:
- 09:16 - kubectl set image deployment/model-proxy-main model-proxy=ghcr.io/redwood-inference/model-proxy:v2.14.0 -n prod
- 09:17 - kubectl rollout status deployment/model-proxy-main -n prod
  -> rollout complete, new pods with v2.14.0 became Ready by 09:20.
- 09:22 - routing layer updated to route 100% to stable, canary scaled to 0 replicas.
- Post-rollback metrics: p95 latency back to ~140ms, 5xxs dropped to baseline.

What went wrong (current working theory):
- v2.14.1-canary changed default pool/concurrency flags which increased connection rate to model-server beyond what its DB-backed resources could handle -> model-server started failing readiness/ooms -> proxy returned upstream errors and 503s.
- The image itself likely fine (no bad binary), but config change not properly validated in perf env.

Short-term mitigation checklist (what we did / should be done):
- Rollback completed (done).
- Open PR to revert the default flag change (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/848) -> link in linked_artifacts.
- Mark v2.14.1-canary tag as quarantined in registry and add note to release artifacts: RE-2341.
- Alerted platform teams to check DB connection pool settings on model-server and consider increasing capacity for next canary.
- Add pre-rollout load test in pipeline: simulate 2x concurrency for 60s against staging model-server to catch pool-exhaust issues.

Longer-term followups / TODOs:
- Add a lint to CI that flags changes to default concurrency/pool flags for proxy/service binaries unless explicitly approved (ownership check).
- Add automated canary smoke test that verifies upstream connections from canary pods to a test harness (basic conv to model-server) before traffic shift.
- Ship a small telemetry change: expose upstream connection fail count via /metrics so canary health checks can detect this pattern earlier.
- Postmortem: RE-2341 assigned to Marcus Rivera. Draft a one-pager with timeline + root cause + action items.

Repro steps (minimal):
- In staging: tag image with same flags (set --pool-size=50) and deploy to 10% traffic; monitor model-server DB pool and readiness for 10 min.
- Commands to simulate load: siege -c100 -t30S http://<canary-ip>/infer (or a simple python script with 200 concurrent requests)

Notes to self / gotchas:
- Helm chart value "proxy.poolSize" was not gated by CI checks -> can be changed by devs without perf review.
- We observed intermittent image pull errors during the incident window; evidence suggests registry throttling in parallel with rollout; add retry/backoff in deployment job.
- Keep a copy of the failing image digest (sha256:abc123...) in the release artifact ticket for later forensic reproduction.

Immediate next actions assigned:
- Marcus: start postmortem doc + tag RE-2341 as high priority.
- Samir: add quick canary smoke check to the argo pipeline (1-hour spike test).
- Me (Ava): quarantine image in registry and open revert PR (linked).

If anyone continues debugging from this note: check model-server logs for DB pool errors around 09:10-09:20 UTC, and validate that the canary image env flags differ from stable. Reproduce in staging before attempting another canary.

Scratch / raw commands to rerun locally (history):
- kubectl logs -n prod -l app=model-proxy -c model-proxy --since=30m > /tmp/mp-logs.txt
- kubectl exec -it <canary-pod> -n prod -- env | grep UPSTREAM
- docker pull ghcr.io/redwood-inference/model-proxy:v2.14.1-canary && docker save | sha256sum (to record digest locally)
- helm rollback model-proxy-main 2 --namespace prod  # used for earlier test rollback in staging

End of breadcrumbs.

(Will convert into a short postmortem draft once Marcus fills timeline gaps.)
